findings.description: completeSetup() calls eel.complete_first_run_setup() and browseDirectory() calls eel.browse_directory() without verifying Eel is connected. Add a check for typeof eel !== 'undefined' before calling, or gracefully handle the error.

The GetSize macro at line ~280 pops three values (SIZE_KB, SIZE_MB, SIZE_GB) but the GetSize function at line ~295 only pushes one value (KB). Stack mismatch causes undefined behavior. Change the macro to pop only SIZE_KB and remove $1 $2 from invocation at line ~155.

platform.js line 75 applies body.classList.add('platform-mac'), but CSS selectors at line ~1100 use .platform-windows and .platform-linux (body selectors) vs .platform-mac .app-header (descendant selector). Pattern is inconsistent for future rules.

filterAndRenderEntries() line ~240 resets filteredEntries but doesn't reset currentOffset. If a user loads 200 entries, filters to 50, then scrolls to bottom, lazy load requests entries 200-250 from backend (unfiltered), not the filtered set. Offset management is confusing when filters are active.

File was truncated at line 950 in the read output. The second half includes _create_task_summary, _save_task_to_history, _get_error_suggestion, and configuration watcher logic which weren't reviewed. Request a re-read to verify those functions don't have import errors, reference non-existent attributes, or call missing Eel functions.

findings.issue: Linux desktop entry CLI flags not implemented
findings.description: linux.desktop Actions section references --new-window and --settings CLI flags. gui_app.py was truncated before argument parsing code, couldn't verify implementation. If flags aren't implemented, remove the Actions section or add argument parsing.

validateCurrentStep() line ~230 returns true for step 1 and step 3. If a user clicks Back from step 4 to step 2, then Next without re-testing, isUrlValidated remains true from previous test. If user edited endpoint after testing, validation is stale. However, isUrlValidated is cleared on endpoint input change (line ~190), so this is not a bug, just subtle flow.

handleProgressUpdate() line ~90 queues updates and sets updateBatchTimeout = true. processPendingUpdates() sets updateBatchTimeout = null at end. A third call arriving right after processPendingUpdates() runs but before next frame could schedule duplicate RAF. Current logic is correct because updateBatchTimeout is checked immediately, but the comment at line ~95 is accurate.
